The Bellman expectation equation

Lesson 25 said a value is the expected reward now plus the discounted value later. Writing that expectation out, over the policy's actions and then over what the ice does, gives the Bellman expectation equation. A backup diagram draws it as a tree.

Pick a cell. Cells show $v_\pi$.

The maths

Start from Lesson 25 and expand the expectation in two layers. First the policy picks $a$ with probability $\pi(a \mid s)$. Then the environment picks the next state and reward with probability $p(s', r \mid s, a)$:

$$v_\pi(s) = \sum_a \pi(a \mid s) \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\,\big[r + \gamma\, v_\pi(s')\big]$$

This is the Bellman expectation equation for $v_\pi$. Read from the inside out: score each outcome by reward plus discounted next value, average over outcomes to get an action's value, then average over actions.

The inner sum is the action value, which Lesson 22 defined by episodes and which this equation computes from $v_\pi$:

$$q_\pi(s, a) = \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\,\big[r + \gamma\, v_\pi(s')\big]$$

The outer sum is then Lesson 23's average, $v_\pi(s) = \sum_a \pi(a \mid s)\, q_\pi(s, a)$. Substituting that into the line above gives the same equation for action values:

$$q_\pi(s, a) = \sum_{s', r} p(s', r \mid s, a)\Big[r + \gamma \sum_{a'} \pi(a' \mid s')\, q_\pi(s', a')\Big]$$

"Backing up" means moving value information from the leaves (successor states) to the root (the current state). The tree above is S&B's backup diagram for $v_\pi$: open circles are states, solid dots are state–action pairs.

There is one equation per non-terminal state, 16 here, each linear in the unknowns $v_\pi(\cdot)$. With $\gamma < 1$ the system has exactly one solution, and it is $v_\pi$. The zero values fail it; the exact ones pass with a gap of 0 everywhere. Lessons 27 and 28 solve such systems directly.
